abstract_sentences.text: Understanding how the brain encodes visual information is a central challenge in neuroscience and machine learning.
abstract_sentences.relation: sets the neuroscience and machine-learning scope

evidence.anchor: central challenge in neuroscience and machine learning

abstract_sentences.text: A promising approach is to reconstruct visual stimuli—essentially images—from functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (fMRI) signals.
abstract_sentences.relation: narrows the scope to fMRI-to-image reconstruction

evidence.anchor: reconstruct visual stimuli from fMRI signals

abstract_sentences.text: This involves two stages: transforming fMRI signals into a latent space and then using a pre-trained generative model to reconstruct images.
abstract_sentences.relation: decomposes the task into representation and generation

abstract_sentences.text: The reconstruction quality depends on how similar the latent space is to the structure of neural activity and how well the generative model produces images from that space.
abstract_sentences.relation: identifies alignment and generation as the two determinants

abstract_sentences.text: Yet, it remains unclear which type of latent space best supports this transformation and how it should be organized to represent visual stimuli effectively.
abstract_sentences.relation: states the unresolved latent-space choice and organization

evidence.anchor: remains unclear which type of latent space

abstract_sentences.text: First, fMRI signals are more similar to the text space of a language model than to either a vision-based space or a joint text–image space.
abstract_sentences.relation: first finding motivates pure text as the bridge

evidence.anchor: more similar to the text space

abstract_sentences.text: Second, text representations and the generative model should be adapted to capture the compositional nature of visual stimuli, including objects, their detailed attributes, and relationships.
abstract_sentences.relation: turns the first finding into a compositional design requirement

abstract_sentences.text: Building on these insights, we propose PRISM, a model that Projects fMRI sIgnals into a Structured text space as an interMediate representation for visual stimuli reconstruction.
abstract_sentences.relation: names the bridge that implements both findings

abstract_sentences.text: It includes an object-centric diffusion module that generates images by composing individual objects to reduce object detection errors, and an attribute/relationship search module that automatically identifies key attributes and relationships that best align with the neural activity.
abstract_sentences.relation: expands PRISM into its two mechanism-bearing modules

abstract_sentences.text: Extensive experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate that our framework outperforms existing methods, achieving up to an 6% reduction in perceptual loss.

evidence.anchor: up to an 6% reduction in perceptual loss

abstract_sentences.text: These results highlight the importance of using structured text as an intermediate space to bridge fMRI signals and image reconstruction.
abstract_sentences.relation: raises the benchmark result to a design implication

evidence.anchor: structured text as an intermediate space

abstract_sentences.relation: provides a code route; §8 uses future-tense release wording

claim_closure.claim: fMRI need not use an image latent; LM text is more aligned.

claim_closure.claim: Visual composition requires object, attribute, and relationship structure.
claim_closure.method_response: Uses object tuples, PropBank headers, per-object MLPs, locations, and spatial concatenation.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 3, Figure 4, and Table 5 support the mechanism, with m settings in Appendix H.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: §6 restates explicit modeling of compositional structure.

claim_closure.claim: Object-centric diffusion is an essential component.
claim_closure.method_response: Uses separate cross-attention conditions and Eq. (6)–(7) spatial/global blending.
claim_closure.evidence_response: w/o ObjC. falls on all three Table 5 metrics on NSD.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: §6 names object-centric diffusion as a specialized module.

claim_closure.claim: Attribute/relationship search finds a useful brain-aligned prompt.
claim_closure.method_response: Eq. (3) and Algorithm 1 optimize similarity under a CKA filter.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Table 5, Table 6, Table 9, and ROI-gradient analysis provide bounded evidence.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: §6 names automatic discovery of aligned attributes/relationships.

claim_closure.claim: PRISM outperforms existing methods and reduces LPIPS by up to 6%.

claim_closure.evidence_response: Table 2 reports three datasets and five metrics; the up-to claim is arithmetically visible for NSD LPIPS.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: §6 repeats the up-to-6% bounded benchmark result.

reduces perceptual loss by up to 6%

claim_closure.conclusion_response: §6 calls structured text a powerful bridge.

final_judgment.single_storyline: The paper treats fMRI-to-image decoding as latent alignment followed by object/attribute binding, selects LM text with CKA/CCA/Generalization Gap, and adds object-centric diffusion plus keyword search (PDF pp.3–6).
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: RQ1–RQ3, three datasets/five metrics, shared SD2.1, Tables 1–6, Eqs. (1)–(7), negative-prompt control, and main component ablations remain in the body (PDF pp.4–10).
final_judgment.appendix_moves: Appendix A–L hold diffusion preliminaries, split counts, baseline adaptation, schedules, Algorithm 1, cross-dataset latent results, object-count/failure cases, prompts, and LLM declaration; seeds and participant count remain absent (PDF pp.17–25).
final_judgment.best_pattern: Figure 1 makes description generation, fMRI-to-text, object-wise cross-attention, and spatial concatenation traceable; Table 1 plus Table 5 connect space choice to module necessity (PDF pp.3–5, p.8).
final_judgment.largest_gap: The QA “significantly” claim lacks a test protocol; high/low-level text claims lack decomposition; ROI interpretation needs neuroscience validation; fixed m=2, 667-image search, SDXL coverage, and LPIPS spread discrepancies weaken closure (PDF pp.7–9, pp.21–22).
final_judgment.transfer_rule: For an intermediate-representation and modular-generation contribution, keep representation comparability, deletion tests, cross-dataset checks, adverse cases, aggregation unit, and uncertainty in one causal chain (PDF pp.4, 7–8, 20).
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: This rule fits decomposable decoding/generation pipelines; other tasks still need a minimal falsifiable contrast rather than mechanically copying CKA, object-count, or prompt-search components (PDF pp.2–6).
